prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t definitively name a single “best” agent for Pleasanton — the right agent depends on your priorities (price, speed, level of hand‑holding, cost, etc.) and the specifics of your house and neighborhood. I can, however, help you find the best one for your situation. To start, tell me the address (or at least the sub‑neighborhood) and what matters most to you, or use the guidance below to choose.

How to find the best agent for your house
- Define your priorities: top sales price, sell quickly, low commission, expertise with luxury/condo/farm, strong digital marketing, relocation experience, etc.
- Look at measurable performance:
  - Recent comps sold in Pleasanton and in your immediate neighborhood
  - List‑to‑sale price ratio and average days on market for the agent
  - Number of transactions in the last 12 months (and in your price range/neighborhood)
- Check sources: MLS performance (if accessible), Realtor.com, Zillow reviews, Redfin, local brokerage pages, and Alameda County records.
- Ask for references from recent sellers (preferably in your neighborhood).
- Interview 3 agents and compare their CMAs and marketing plans.

What to ask when you interview agents
- What comparable homes did you use to price my home? What price range do you recommend and why?
- What was the sale price vs. list price and DOM for those comps?
- How many homes have you sold in my neighborhood/price range in the last year?
- What is your marketing plan (photos, video, staging, paid ads, open houses, social media, email lists)?
- Who will be my main point of contact? Will you use a team?
- What is your commission and are you open to negotiation? Any other fees I should expect?
- Can you provide references from recent sellers and examples of marketing materials?
- How will you handle offers and negotiation strategy?

Red flags to avoid
- Vague or overly generic CMAs
- No recent sales in your neighborhood or price range
- Unwillingness to put a marketing plan in writing
- Poor online reviews that repeat the same serious complaints
- High-pressure tactics to sign an exclusive listing quickly without data

Local places to research agents
- Pleasanton Chamber of Commerce
- Realtor.com and Zillow agent profiles & reviews
- Local brokerages with strong Tri‑Valley presence (Keller Williams Tri‑Valley, Intero Real Estate, Coldwell Banker, Compass, Redfin, Century 21) — check each agent’s local track record
- Alameda County property records and MLS snapshots

If you want, I can:
- Pull a short list of top Pleasanton agents based on recent publicly available sales (tell me your address or neighborhood), or
- Draft an email you can send to 3 agents to request CMAs and marketing plans, or
- Provide a customizable interview script.

Which of those would you like me to do next?
